audit.why: 49.99% over 4543 games — the flattest matchup in this slice. Brief and packet agree. No writable text quotes a win rate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Worst chart corruption of the three pages: FIVE of seven rows wrong. packet.levelChart = [Darius, Darius, Darius, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax]. content win[] and full phases[].side both read [Darius, Darius, Skill, Darius, Skill, Darius, Darius]. Rows 4-5, first item and 2+ items literally say 'Darius' while the why printed on the same row says Jax wins it.
audit.why: Row-by-row the whys contradict their own cells: whys[3] 'Level 4 E Counter Strike stun-and-dodge flips trades to Jax' (cell says Darius), whys[4] 'the level-6 all-in his' (cell says Skill), whys[5] 'His BotRK/Trinity spike out-sustains your bleed at first item' (cell says Darius), whys[6] 'Full-build E, R resists, and Q gap-close win him every late duel' (cell says Darius). Every prose field agrees with the packet too: early 'Levels 1-3 are your only real edge', mid 'From level 4 Jax takes over', late 'Full-build Jax wins the duel', spikes[0] 'Your only clear window is levels 1-3', spikes[1] 'By 6 this is Jax's lane', spikes[2] 'Jax's ... spike beats yours', spikes[3] 'Fully itemized Jax wins the duel outright'. Eleven statements against five cells, and the corrected shape is also the only one consistent with a 49.99% win rate on a champion who scales.
audit.corrected: Chart set to packet shape on both layers: Darius / Darius / Darius / Jax / Jax / Jax / Jax. phases[3].why, phases[4].why, phases[5].why and phases[6].why all rewritten because each argued Darius on a row that now reads Jax. All flips proposed as one group. Ratings not touched — polarity ambiguous, see questionsForUser.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 and late spikes are built on 'R Grandmaster's Might'. That is not the ability's name. The packet and the kit both give Jax's R as Grandmaster-at-Arms. The wrong name appears in whys[4], spikes[1].text, content.mid and wants.foe[1].
audit.why: Exactly the calibration case in the brief — a stale ability name presented as current. Grandmaster's Might is the pre-rework name; a player searching it finds nothing that matches what is happening to him. Real spike shape: Darius owns levels 1-3 only; Jax spikes at 4 (Counter Strike), 6 (Grandmaster-at-Arms, 110s), first item, and full build.
audit.corrected: All four occurrences replaced with Grandmaster-at-Arms. whys[4] and wants.foe[1] are exact-length swaps. spikes[1].text and content.mid rewritten around it, and spikes[1] now carries the 110s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions missing, one of them the whole matchup. (1) Counter Strike 'allows him to dodge all incoming ATTACKS'. Darius's Decimate (Q) is an ability, not an attack, so it lands through an active Counter Strike — while Crippling Strike (W), which explicitly modifies 'Darius's next attack', gets dodged along with his autos. The page says 'never combo into an active E' as if the whole kit is nullified. (2) Grandmaster-at-Arms increases Armor and Magic Resist, but Noxian Guillotine deals TRUE damage — 'ignores armour and MR, resistances do not help'. His defensive ultimate does nothing to your execute. Neither appears in any writable field.
audit.why: (1) turns a dead ~2 seconds into a free Decimate every time he panics his E, which is the difference between baiting and hiding. (2) reverses the level-6 advice: the page implies you should not commit into his ult, when in fact the execute is precisely the tool his ult cannot answer. Also relevant and absent: Apprehend's passive makes Darius's physical damage ignore a percentage of the target's Armor, which partly offsets the Armor half of his ult, and Leap Strike targets ANY unit, so minions and wards are stepping stones — the mobility denial is about fighting away from the wave.
audit.corrected: Attacks-vs-abilities written into tldr, report[0].t, report[5].t, dontsFull[0].d, breakdown.early and content.mid. True-damage-vs-resists written into phases[4].why and spikes[1].text. Leap Strike's any-unit targeting written into spikes[0].text, spikes[3].text, dontsFull[2].d and breakdown.cooldowns. Real cooldowns throughout: Counter Strike 17s rank 1 / 9s rank 5 and 300 range, Leap Strike 6-8s and 700 range, Grandmaster-at-Arms 110/100/90, Apprehend 26s rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeGood and dosFull[1].d carry the same templated pull line with no reference to the one cooldown that governs whether the trade is safe.
audit.why: Against Jax the trade rule is not about stack count, it is about leaving before Counter Strike is back. Anchoring the exit to his E rather than to a stack number makes the same-length line correct.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to end 'leave before his E comes back', with the Q blade-edge heal named.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained not one Jax number — just 'Bait it; never combo into an active E' followed by the same duplicated Apprehend/Ghost paragraph that appears on every page in this slice.
audit.why: Counter Strike going from 17s at rank 1 to 9s at rank 5 is the arc of the entire matchup: early you can wait it out, late you cannot. A cooldowns field that omits that number omits the reason Darius loses this lane over time.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Counter Strike 17s/9s and its 300-unit stun radius, Leap Strike 6-8s targeting any unit, Grandmaster-at-Arms 110/100/90, and Apprehend 26s tied to his Q being down.

audit.why: Freeze-outside-turret is right, and it gains a second justification from the kit: a frozen wave near your tower is a wave Jax must approach, and fighting off the minion line denies Leap Strike its jump target. breakdown.wave carries the duplicated paragraph plus a spliced 'How Darius Wins Trades' heading, but the wave advice itself is sound and I had no length-safe replacement.
Ganking on Counter Strike's cooldown is the right trigger; with E down his only escape is a 700-range Leap Strike that still needs a unit to target.
Conqueror plus Second Wind / Bone Plating is coherent. Nothing verifiable from the kits to change.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.early instructs 'Anti-heal his late sustain'. Jax has no healing anywhere in his kit — Relentless Assault is Attack Speed, Leap Strike is a leap and a strike, Empower is bonus damage, Counter Strike is dodge and stun, Grandmaster-at-Arms is magic damage and resists. Correspondingly, Jax is the one matchup in this slice with NO needs-antiheal entry in missingInteractions.
audit.why: Telling a Darius to buy Grievous Wounds against a champion with no kit heal wastes an item slot in a matchup he is already losing on scaling. Any Jax sustain is item lifesteal, which is a different purchase decision and not something the kit files establish.
audit.corrected: The anti-heal instruction removed from breakdown.early and replaced with the Counter Strike bait sequence. No Grievous Wounds advice added anywhere on this page.

audit.why: 'Bait E, pull, bleed, execute' is the correct win condition and survives the corrections intact — the edits just make each verb mechanically executable.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four of six Do/Don't bodies mismatch their titles — the same three template strings as the other two pages. dontsFull[0] 'Auto into his active E' had generic filler. dontsFull[1] 'Extend his level-6 spike' had the committal-tool line. dontsFull[2] 'Fight him even late' had the whiffed-Apprehend line. dosFull[2] 'R at 5 stacks' had a line about him wasting Counter Strike.
audit.why: Each title names a real mechanic the kit can explain and each body was filled with unrelated boilerplate. dosFull[2] in particular was the natural home for the flagged Empower auto-reset tell and instead held a duplicate of the 'Great trade' line.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[0].d now contrasts attacks with Decimate. dontsFull[1].d names Grandmaster-at-Arms's resists and the Attack Speed passive. dontsFull[2].d names the 700-range any-unit Leap Strike. dosFull[0].d gives the concrete bait-and-step-out sequence with the 17s number. dosFull[2].d carries the Empower wind-up tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: Empower (W) carries a derived 'dash: mobility that grounding and walls can deny' flag. Riot's text is 'Jax charges his weapon with energy, causing his next attack to deal additional damage' — there is no movement in it at all. Jax's only dash is Leap Strike (Q). Separately, spikes[2].text asserts Counter Strike has a '~2s window'; no duration appears anywhere in the kit data.
audit.why: The W dash flag is a clean tooltip-parsing misfire and, unlike the Illaoi case, it is contradicted by an ability that plainly has no movement component. On the duration: I removed the '~2s' rather than keep an unverifiable number, and replaced the advice with the verified 300-unit stun radius, which gives the player an actual distance to walk instead of a stopwatch.
audit.corrected: No text treats Empower as mobility. The '~2s window' removed from spikes[2].text and replaced with 'step out of its 300 range'. W is described only as an attack modifier and burst tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: No patch anchoring available; kits carry no patch metadata.
audit.why: Live patch is 26.15. I did not research patch history, so I left every patch-sensitive claim untouched rather than date-stamp anything unverified. Worth noting the page's item references (Blade of the Ruined King / Trinity, Stridebreaker, Sterak's, Dead Man's Plate) are unverified against the current patch by me.

edits.before: Your only clear window is levels 1-3, before Jax has his combo: E Apprehend him, W Crippling Strike, and stack Hemorrhage while his Q Leap Strike has nothing to jump to if you sit on the wave. Once he hits level 4 with E Counter Strike his stun-and-dodge flips trades, so front-load your aggression early.
edits.after: Your only clear window is levels 1-3, before Counter Strike exists at 4: Apprehend him, Crippling Strike, and stack Hemorrhage. Leap Strike targets any unit, so fight him away from the minions — with nothing to jump to, his 700-range escape is gone and he has to stand in your bleed.

edits.before: By 6 this is Jax's lane: his R Grandmaster's Might resists plus E Counter Strike stun mean an even all-in goes his way. Don't trade into an active E — his dodge negates your autos and the stun lets him W and reset. Only R Guillotine him if he's already burned E and is genuinely low, or you'll get stunned mid-combo and die.
edits.after: By 6 this is Jax's lane: Grandmaster-at-Arms (110s) adds Armor and Magic Resist on top of the Counter Strike stun. But those resists do nothing to Noxian Guillotine — it is true damage. So the execute still kills him; what you cannot do is brawl through his ult, because his passive climbs Attack Speed every auto.

edits.before: Jax's Blade of the Ruined King/Trinity spike beats yours — his on-hit DPS and R resists out-sustain your bleed in a prolonged fight. Stop face-checking him; wait out E Counter Strike (dodge it by walking away for the ~2s window) before you even consider committing, and lean on jungle pressure instead.
edits.after: Jax's first item beats yours — Relentless Assault stacks Attack Speed on consecutive autos, so every second the fight runs he hits harder while your bleed stays flat. Keep it short: bait Counter Strike, step out of its 300 range, land your damage, and disengage before his ult resists come up.

edits.before: Fully itemized Jax wins the duel outright: R gives him massive bonus resists, E stuns your all-in, and his Q gap-close means you can't disengage. Don't split-push into him at even gold — group, save E-pull to peel him off a carry, and only fight when his E is down and he's already low.
edits.after: Fully itemized Jax wins the duel outright: Grandmaster-at-Arms adds Armor and MR, Counter Strike is down to 9s so waiting it out barely helps, and Leap Strike reaches 700 units off any unit. Don't split into him at even gold — group and save Apprehend to peel him off a carry.

edits.before: From level 4 Jax takes over: E Counter Strike dodges your autos and stuns you, and by 6 R Grandmaster's Might resists make an even all-in his. Never commit into an active E — walk out its window first, and only ult him if he's already low with E on cooldown.
edits.after: From level 4 Jax takes over: Counter Strike dodges attacks and stuns, and by 6 Grandmaster-at-Arms resists blunt your bleed. Never auto into an active E — Decimate still lands through it, so Q while you walk out, then ult once the stun is spent.

notes:
STALE ABILITY NAME, likely repo-wide: 'Grandmaster's Might' is Jax's pre-rework R name and appeared in four fields on this page. The packet's suspectNames array is EMPTY for this matchup, so the near-miss detector did not catch it — it only flags misspellings, not correct-but-obsolete names. Any other Darius page referencing Jax, and any Jax-owned page, is worth grepping for 'Grandmaster's Might'.

FABRICATED SUSTAIN: breakdown.early told the player to 'Anti-heal his late sustain'. Jax's kit contains no heal of any kind, and he is the only enemy in this slice with no needs-antiheal entry in missingInteractions — the data and the text disagree, and the data is right. Removed.

FLAG MISFIRE: Empower (W) carries a 'dash' flag against a description with no movement in it ('causing his next attack to deal additional damage'). Jax's only dash is Leap Strike. Third flag misfire across three matchups (Illaoi R grounding/untargetable, Irelia E grounding, Jax W dash) — the derived-flag pass looks unreliable enough that it should not be trusted unreviewed anywhere.

SCRAPE ARTIFACT: 'Darius Top Lane Matchup Database 22' sits mid-sentence inside breakdown.trading here, matching '88'/'89' on Irelia and '73' on Illaoi. breakdown.wave and report[4].t additionally have a 'How Darius Wins Trades' heading spliced into the middle of the wave paragraph. I only cleaned breakdown.cooldowns; breakdown.trading, breakdown.wave and report[4].t still carry it.

Unverified duration removed rather than kept: spikes[2] claimed Counter Strike has a '~2s window'. No duration exists in the kit data, so I replaced the stopwatch advice with the verified 300-unit stun radius.
